refnamediv.refpurpose: Stream error handling context option listing

refentry.refsect1:
&reftitle.description;
The options under the stream key are available for all wrappers. They control how the errors of stream operations that use the context are reported. See for an overview.

&reftitle.options;
error_mode StreamErrorMode
How errors are reported: as diagnostics such as E_WARNING (StreamErrorMode::Error), by throwing a StreamException for terminating errors (StreamErrorMode::Exception), or not at all (StreamErrorMode::Silent).
Defaults to StreamErrorMode::Error.
error_store StreamErrorStore
Which errors are stored for retrieval with stream_last_errors.
Defaults to StreamErrorStore::Auto, which stores no errors with StreamErrorMode::Error, the non-terminating errors with StreamErrorMode::Exception, and all errors with StreamErrorMode::Silent.
error_handler callable
A callback that is called once for every operation that reported errors, with the following signature:
voidhandler arrayerrors
errors
A list of StreamError objects with all errors of the operation, in the order in which they were reported.
The handler is called regardless of error_store, after the errors have been reported as diagnostics. It is not called if a StreamException is thrown. Its return value is ignored.

&reftitle.errors;
The values of these options are not validated when the context is created. If an operation reports an error and error_mode is not a StreamErrorMode, error_store is not a StreamErrorStore, or error_handler is not a valid callable, a TypeError is thrown.
